## 7f31c4f794b2

**Reproduced undeclared shape-conditioned shortcut.** Audited generator SHA-256:
`4e3177bab6a537619394175d91588775cc0b9a60c7b520387fc27e4b53f9c87d`.
Executed rule hash: `187a145d27eb`. The target was not modified.

Rival rule: recolor a component to 7 when it touches the border **unless it is a
T tetromino**. This rival matches all four canonical training pairs and the one
canonical test pair because no canonical border component is T-shaped. The
generator’s documented shape family includes T4, although no canonical border
component is T-shaped; shape gating is therefore a plausible object shortcut
rather than a pure lookup.

A deterministic search over the target's actual sampler found difficulty `easy`,
seed `30`, sample indices `0,1,2,3`. The first three generated pairs contain no
border T tetromino, so the rival matches all three exact Racket labels; at least
one demonstration contains an *interior* T tetromino, reinforcing the false
shape gate. The query contains a border-touching color-9 T tetromino. Exact Racket
recolors its four cells to 7, while the rival leaves them 9 at `(9,6)`, `(10,5)`,
`(10,6)`, and `(11,6)`. All four generated inputs pass `self_check`.

Evidence:

- `checks/audit/7f31c4f794b2/search_shape_shortcut.py`
- `checks/audit/7f31c4f794b2/search_report.json`

Suggested repair: add shape-conditioned survivors derived from the canonical
shape family to `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, then require each lesson to demonstrate a
border T4 (or otherwise refute every surviving shape gate). The existing four
rivals and 1,200 rotation census remain useful, but they do not cover this rule.
